abstract: We investigate the algorithmic structure of a deterministic brute-force attack on a simulated smart lock implemented in pure Python. The lock stores a numeric PIN and exposes a single \texttt{unlock(attempt)} operation. We formalize the lock's state machine, prove that the attack preserves linearizability, and analyze its asymptotic complexity. Empirical measurements on an AMD EPYC 7763 platform (1 physical core, 2 logical threads, 7.8~GB RAM, Chronos-Architecture 7.0.0-1017-azure) show a mean latency of 51 127.56 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 19 559 ops/s over 30 iterations. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261029_130130_keyless_entry__hacking_switchb}.
